functions.name: daisy
functions.done: Euclidean, Manhattan, Gower, and standardized Euclidean. The triangle is read by rows.

proof.python:
import json
import statistics
import sys
import time

sys.path[:0] = ["/home/ahmed/killr_projects/killr/packages/cluster"]
from cluster import daisy, lower_to_upper_tri_inds, meanabsdev, size_diss, upper_to_lower_tri_inds

rows = [[1, 2], [3, 6], [4, 8], [7, 1]]

def one():
    return daisy(rows) + daisy(rows, metric="manhattan") + daisy(rows, metric="gower") + daisy(rows, stand=True)

value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
if not isinstance(value, list):
    value = [value]
print(json.dumps({"value": value, "median_ms": statistics.median(elapsed)}))

functions.name: clusplot
functions.done: Distances and shading of a daisy dissimilarity. A missing shade, which R stores as NA, is compared as -1.

proof.r:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(cluster))
if (packageDescription("cluster")$Version != "2.1.8.3") stop("expected cluster 2.1.8.3")
options(warn = -1)
json_num <- function(x) paste0("[", paste(sprintf("%.17g", as.numeric(x)), collapse=","), "]")
x <- matrix(c(1,2, 1.2,1.8, 1.1,2.2, 5,8, 5.5,7.5, 4.8,8.2, 9,1, 8.5,1.5, 8.2,1.2, 5.2,7.8), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)

one <- function() {
  fit <- pam(x, 3)
  pdf(NULL)
  drawn <- clusplot(daisy(x), fit$clustering, diss = TRUE, span = TRUE, lines = 2)
  dev.off()
  shade <- drawn$Shading
  shade[is.na(shade)] <- -1
  c(as.numeric(drawn$Distances), shade)
}
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
cat(sprintf('{"value":%s,"median_ms":%.17g}\n', json_num(value), median(elapsed) * 1000))

import json
import math
import statistics
import sys
import time

sys.path[:0] = ["/home/ahmed/killr_projects/killr/packages/cluster"]
from cluster import (
    agnes, clara, coef_hclust, coef_hier, diana, fanny, max_se, medoids,
    mona, pam, silhouette, sort_silhouette,
)
from cluster.twins import as_hclust

def one():
    x = [[0, 0], [0.1, 0], [0.2, 0.1], [5, 5], [5, 6], [5.2, 4.8]]
    n = len(x)
    matrix = [[0.0] * n for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            distance = math.dist(x[i], x[j])
            matrix[i][j] = matrix[j][i] = distance
    fit = silhouette(pam(x, 2)["clustering"], dmatrix=matrix)
    return [row[1] for row in fit["widths"]] + [row[2] for row in fit["widths"]]
value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(json.dumps({"value": value, "median_ms": statistics.median(elapsed)}))
